form.name: Name
form.exprHelp:
Optional. A condition evaluated on top of the match above — BOTH must pass for the rule to apply.
Variables: w (1 = next turn likely writes / calls a tool, else 0) · t (predicted output tokens) · tokens (input prompt tokens) · group (key's group) · model (requested model).
Operators: == != < <= > >=  combine with && (and) || (or) ! (not) and ( ).
Note: using w or t invokes the small-model router classifier once per request; other variables add no latency.
form.targetGroup: Or target group (optional alternative to channels)
form.targetModelPlaceholder: leave empty to keep the requested model
form.targetModelHelp:
Optional. When set, matched requests are served by this model instead of the one the client asked for — that is how one channel can serve several difficulty tiers (e.g. opus for hard requests, haiku for easy ones).
The target channel's model mapping still applies on top of it, so use the external model name here, not the upstream id.
form.targetModelNotServed: None of the selected target channels lists "{{value}}" in its models. You can still save (the channel may be configured later), but until one serves it, matched requests will fail with no-candidate-channel.
form.targetModelSuggestTitle: Models served by the selected channels (click to use):

exprEx.write: next turn likely calls a tool / writes code
exprEx.longWrite: tool call AND a long predicted output
exprEx.vipOrWrite: VIP key, or any tool-call turn
exprEx.modelAndWrite: a specific model doing a tool call
exprEx.midTier: difficulty tiering — mid tier: a tool call or a medium-length output (pair with a target model such as sonnet, and let a lower-priority catch-all rule route the rest to a cheaper one)

target.modelTooltip: This rule overrides the model: matched requests are served by this model instead of the one the client requested.

validation.targetRequired: Select at least one target channel or a target group.

probe.title: Routing classifier (small-model probe)
probe.help: Routing expressions that use w or t need a classifier to predict them. Mock = built-in heuristic, no external call (good for trying rules). Real = POST each prediction to your HTTP proxy in front of the SageMaker endpoint.
